theDefectAsTheDispatchStatesItAndAsReMea.asStated: `issue()` spawned `argv[0]` by bare name; on Windows `gcloud`/`vercel` are `.cmd` shims Node cannot spawn without a shell, and `err.status` is null on a spawn error so the failure rendered as `FAILED (exit ?)`.
theDefectAsTheDispatchStatesItAndAsReMea.theOneWordFixIsADeadEnd: `{shell: true}` works and is why it is the obvious answer. It is refused here because it concatenates: with a shell the argv is no longer passed as an array, so a commit, a project name or a service name carrying a space, a quote or a semicolon can be re-split into additional flags, and Node itself warns (DEP0190). The header of the file being repaired exists to state that no shell string is ever built. A fix that discards the property the file is proudest of would be a fix that moves the defect.

theChoiceAndWhy.chosen: The FIRST of the two repairs the dispatch allows -- resolve the executable explicitly so the argv stays an array. No shell string is built on any path.
theChoiceAndWhy.notChosen: The second repair -- keep a shell and earn it by asserting each value against its allowed pattern -- is strictly weaker (it survives only because the values are already constrained) and would still concatenate. It was not needed once the first repair was measured to work against the real CLIs.
theChoiceAndWhy.theAspotThatIsNotObvious: The `.cmd` cannot be spawned directly (EINVAL), so it is run through `cmd.exe`. The question is then WHICH string is handed to `cmd.exe` as the program. Measured: it must be the BARE NAME, never the resolved absolute path.

theTrapAndHowTheArraySurvives.theMeasurement:
`cmd.exe /d /s /c <argv...>` was driven with this host's own node.exe as the program, both as the resolved absolute path and as a bare name. With the ABSOLUTE PATH it fails: `C:\Program Files
odejs
ode.exe` is re-split at the space into `C:\Program` and `Files
odejs
ode.exe`, because `cmd.exe` parses its own tail. With the BARE NAME it works: `cmd.exe` re-resolves the name through PATH itself and the arguments arrive intact.
theTrapAndHowTheArraySurvives.whyThatMattersHere: This fleet's gcloud shim path itself contains a space (`...\Cloud SDK\...`), so the tempting form -- hand `cmd.exe` the resolved path so nothing is ambiguous -- is exactly the form that breaks. The fix therefore resolves the program on PATH for the DECISION (is it there? is it a shim?) and hands `cmd.exe` the bare name for the EXECUTION.
theTrapAndHowTheArraySurvives.whatIsPreserved: Every argument stays a separate element of the array passed to execFileSync from the plan, through runTool, to the spawn. No string is ever joined and re-split. The `--source <worktree path>`, the `SERVED_COMMIT=<sha>` and the `--update-labels commit-sha=<sha>` values are each one argv element end to end, which the verbatim failure output in CP2 shows printed as single tokens.

theMetacharacterSetAsMeasured.whyThisExists: Routing a shim through `cmd.exe` means `cmd.exe` interprets its tail. Something has to stop a value from becoming a different command, and the list must be the MEASURED dangerous set rather than an assumed one -- a wrong list is a control that cannot fire (too narrow) or one that refuses the fleet's own values (too broad).
theMetacharacterSetAsMeasured.method: `cmd.exe /d /s /c node <probe> <arg>` with a probe that echoes the argv elements it actually received, one character class per run.
theMetacharacterSetAsMeasured.shippedRule: CMD_METACHARACTERS = /[&|%^<>\r\n]/ -- the measured dangerous set plus newlines. Any value carrying one is REFUSED with kind 'refused' and nothing is spawned.
theMetacharacterSetAsMeasured.honestLimit: This set is the set THIS program's arguments need. It is a refusal, not an escaping scheme: an argument the plan ever needs to carry an `&` would be refused and the plan would have to be changed, and the correct response to that would be to review whether the value belongs in an argv array at all. No plan row today carries one.

preRegisteredFalsifiers: F1 THE SPAWN PATH RUNS A REAL TOOL, READ-ONLY, END TO END. `gcloud run services describe <service> --project <project> --region us-east1 --format=value(status.url)` and a read-only `vercel` command, driven through the SHIPPED runTool (not a paraphrase), must each print the tool's own output and exit 0. Would falsify the fix if either exited non-zero for a spawn reason, or if either produced no output. Registered BEFORE the run, and the URL is a fact the tool fetches, not a value this lane supplies.

F2 A TOOL THAT EXISTS RETURNS REAL OUTPUT. The positive self-test leg must spawn a tool that returns a version matching ^\d+\.\d+ on stdout. The leg spawns `npm` deliberately: `npm` is a `.cmd` SHIM on Windows, and the broken code spawned a real executable (`node.exe`) perfectly. A self-test that ran only node.exe would PASS ON THE DEFECT IT EXISTS TO CATCH -- so the not-vacuous case is the point of the leg, not a detail of it.

F3 A TOOL THAT DOES NOT EXIST FAILS WITH A NAMED REASON. The negative leg asserts a ToolFailure of kind `spawn` whose message CONTAINS the absent tool's name and the words 'could not be spawned'. Merely 'it threw' is not a pass: the old code also threw, and rendered as `(exit ?)`. Would falsify the fix if the absent-tool case passed silently, or if it produced an unnamed failure.

F4 THE INSTRUMENT CAN FAIL, PROVEN BY VIOLATION. Revert the spawn to the legacy bare-name call, re-run the self-test: F2's leg must FAIL. Restore: it must PASS. Both runs recorded verbatim in CP2. This is the control on the control -- without it, a self-test that passes because it asserts nothing looks identical to one that passes because the code is right.

F5 THE ERROR MESSAGE NAMES THE KIND. A spawn failure and a non-zero exit must be DISTINGUISHABLE in the output. Exercise the real entry point with the tool unreachable on PATH and assert the message says the tool could not be spawned, names the command being run, and says what to check -- three things `(exit ?)` did not say.

scripts/deploy.mjs (BOTH repos, identica: resolveOnPath(name, {env, platform}) -- EXPORTED. Reads PATH/PATHEXT and stats candidates. Read-only: it spawns nothing. Returns null when absent, which is what lets an absent tool be reported by NAME instead of surfacing cmd.exe's generic 'not recognized'.

runTool(argv, {cwd, stdio, env, platform}) -- EXPORTED, the ONLY place a real tool runs. Refuses a cmd metacharacter (kind 'refused'); resolves the program (kind 'spawn' if absent); routes a .cmd/.bat shim through `cmd.exe /d /s /c <bareName> <args...>`; classifies a thrown error into kind 'exit' when err.status is a number and kind 'spawn' otherwise.
ToolFailure -- EXPORTED. Carries kind ('refused' | 'spawn' | 'exit') and a detail object.
issue(argv, label) -- edited to call runTool and to print what could not be spawned, the command, and what to check, replacing `FAILED (exit ?)`.
selfTest() -- EXPORTED, reachable as `--self-test`. Three legs: F2, F3, F4's metacharacter leg.
The header gains a G-169 paragraph and the CLI line for --self-test.
